cards.issue: Unsupported generalization: "Getting clear early usually creates more options, not fewer."
cards.fix: Getting clear early can leave you more options.

cards.issue: Unsupported frequency claim: "A packed house is often a family matter before it is a real estate matter, and nobody should be judged for it."
cards.fix: A packed house can be a family matter as well as a real estate matter, and you should not feel judged for it.

cards.issue: Unsupported claim about what people do: "Many people in this spot are not avoiding the problem."
cards.fix: You may not be avoiding the problem; the house just feels too heavy to deal with.

hedge.note: No ledger claim or passage supports "often a family matter before it is a real estate matter". Say it can be a family matter, and phrase the not-judging line as a gentle statement to the reader.
No claim supports "usually". Say getting clear early can leave you more options.

cards.issue: Unsupported generalization: "Most families are not looking for judgment."
cards.fix: Speak to the reader instead, e.g. "You are probably looking for time and a clear next step," or drop the sentence.

cards.issue: "Many owners think the clutter has to be explained away..." and "this is often the question that makes people freeze" are unsupported generalizations.
cards.fix: Reword to the reader's situation, e.g. "You may wonder whether the clutter has to be explained or left out."

cards.issue: "The waiver rule means that route is not open" extends clm:7 (waiver void) to hiding disclosure.
cards.fix: Say that skipping disclosure by agreement (a waiver) is void, and point to the agent or attorney for the rest.

cards.issue: Unsupported generalization: "The real question is usually not which route is best."
cards.fix: Drop "usually", e.g. "The question to ask is which route fits your situation."

hedge.note: No ledger claim or passage supports what is "usually" the real question. State it as framing without a frequency claim.

Not a statistic. It restates the approved brief honest_options (each route has a when_it_fits) and the unit itself: four of the five routes are not Twin Home Buyer. No ledger claim is needed; nothing here asserts a count of sellers.

cards.issue: Unsupported generalization: "The real question is usually whether the house or the paperwork is the bigger risk to the sale." and "A lot of it comes from the paperwork and the people."
cards.fix: Say the house, the paperwork and the people can each stall a sale, with no 'usually' and no 'a lot of it'.

cards.issue: "The disclosures are made on the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement form." does not state the single-family residential scope.
cards.fix: Add 'on a sale of single-family residential property' and keep the confirm-with-an-agent-or-attorney line.

hedge.note: No claim or passage supports 'usually'. Say these are things that can stall a sale, without a frequency, and drop 'A lot of it comes from the paperwork and the people'.

cards.issue: Unsupported generalization: "A house full of belongings is hard enough without finding out halfway through that nobody checked who could sign."
cards.fix: Reword as a risk, e.g. a sale can stall if it turns out late that the person planning to sign lacks authority; avoid nobody/no one.

hedge.note: No claim or passage supports 'nobody checked'. Say what is supported: a sale can stall when authority to sign is unclear (brief warning, seller-problem logic), framed as a risk not a fact about people.

cards.issue: Uncited legal conclusion: "Living in the house alone does not give you that authority."
cards.fix: Use "The person living in the house is not always the person with authority to sign." and keep the attorney or title company confirmation.

hedge.note: 'Not always.' is a qualifier, not a legal claim; it is supported by the brief's honest_options (keep_it, fix_it, sell_directly), which show cleanout is not required in every route. No ledger claim is needed.
